source.title: SOTAlign: Semi-Supervised Alignment of Unimodal Vision and Language Models via Optimal Transport
source.authors: Simon Roschmann; Paul Krzakala; Sonia Mazelet; Quentin Bouniot; Zeynep Akata

record.tranche_reason: The study measures how well learned projections align frozen unimodal representations using downstream retrieval and related metrics. This is a conceptual test of whether representations can be mapped into a shared space, not a reproduction of a scale-convergence measurement.
record.gate_note: The paper explicitly motivates its experiments as a test of whether pretrained unimodal encoders have compatible semantic structure. It reports results for learned linear alignment and for semi-supervised alignment across encoder pairs and datasets. It does not measure representational convergence as model scale or capability increases. Cited findings from other work are not included as rows.
record.test_reason: The authors frame the work as a test of the Platonic Representation Hypothesis. They fit linear maps (Procrustes, CCA, contrastive) between frozen unimodal vision, text and speech encoders from few pairs and report cross-modal retrieval, which bears on V4. They also report raw mutual k-NN between frozen DINOv2/DINOv3 and three text encoders, which bears weakly on V2. There is no scale sweep, seed comparison or feature-level analysis.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors also state that linear maps from very few pairs recover meaningful vision-language alignment, which they present as empirical support for the Platonic Representation Hypothesis. They attribute DINOv3's downstream advantage over DINOv2 to its larger pretraining data, citing PRH, and propose mutual k-NN as a fast compatibility diagnostic (r=0.95).
record.recipe_differences: The study trains linear projection layers with paired supervision and a semi-supervised optimal-transport regularizer, then evaluates downstream retrieval or classification. It does not measure raw representation convergence across a scale sweep.
record.method_sensitivity: Performance changes with the number and source of paired and unpaired samples, encoder pair, dataset/domain, and OT regularization settings. The paper reports Pearson r = 0.95 between mutual k-NN and downstream Mean R@1 across encoder pairs, and Pearson r = −0.76 between distribution shift and performance.

fits_no_version.finding: Across encoder pairs including ResNet-50 and BERT, pre-alignment mutual k-NN correlates with post-SOTAlign COCO MeanR@1 (Pearson r = 0.95, Figure 7). Among the six DINO pairs, though, DINOv2 has higher k-NN but lower downstream retrieval than DINOv3.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Mutual k-NN between frozen vision and text encoders predicts how well they can be aligned with few pairs.

record.peer_reviewed: Proceedings of the 43rd International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 306, 2026
record.problems: The main outcomes are downstream retrieval or classification scores after training an alignment layer, not direct measures of spontaneous convergence. The study does not vary model scale or capability systematically, and it does not compare mapped representations with the original encoders' task utility. Retrieval results generally have no uncertainty estimates reported.
record.rows_left_out: Kept 54 rows. Other results on classification datasets and additional training-data-source and robustness conditions (Tables 5, 9, 12 and Appendix B figures) were left out because they report further downstream performance of the alignment method rather than an additional direct measure of representation mapping; the 60-row limit also precluded adding all such conditions.

untested.parts: No sweep of model size or capability; no comparison across architectures or objectives as a function of scale.

Only two vision encoders (DINOv2/DINOv3, same ViT-L size) and three similar top-MMTEB text encoders. There is no systematic capability axis for the text side. The ResNet-50/BERT points appear only in Figure 7, without values in the text.
Untested: paired-data-free mapping, stitching, relative representations, and loss relative to each encoder's native performance.
No features, neurons, SAE features or circuits.
No comparison of similarity metrics or k settings as convergence measures. Distribution-shift results concern training data for the alignment method, not the measured convergence.
No test of plateaus with scale or of shared data or objectives as causes.

missing.what: Standalone CCA linear map, speech-text (WavLM-Large + NV-Embed-v2, 1k pairs): LibriSpeech S2T R@1 72.4, T2S R@1 75.1. This is strong cross-modal linear mappability.
Standalone CCA on SkyScript: T2I R@10 21.0, I2T R@10 21.3
Supervised SAIL linear maps per encoder pair (e.g. 25.4-35.6 ImageNet). These are the purely linear paired-data mappings for each pair.
Linear alignment versus number of pairs, 100 to 100k: both SAIL and SOTAlign fail at 100 pairs
Mutual k-NN and retrieval for weaker encoders (ResNet-50, BERT) in the r=0.95 plot

record.verdict_notes: Key correction: the reader swapped the DINOv2/DINOv3 blocks of Table 10, since rotated labels were extracted in reverse. The default DINOv3+NV-Embed-v2 numbers (SAIL 35.6/21.0/27.4, SOTAlign 46.1/26.5/34.1) confirm the assignment. Corrected, DINOv3 has lower raw mutual k-NN than DINOv2 but better downstream alignment. That cuts against the authors' PRH reading and hints that k-NN and alignability rankings disagree (possible V6 relevance; not labelled). Rows r4-r30 and r37-r54 compare the study's own method with baselines. They are kept for V4 only as absolute levels of linear-layer alignability; their 'baselines' are other alignment methods, not controls for convergence. No uncertainty is reported for any row.

versions.untested_parts: No sweep measures whether independently trained models become more similar as scale or capability increases.
The study aligns image and text representations, but does not measure whether their raw alignment rises as both encoders improve.
No comparison of training seeds or shared features across seeds.

Tests learned linear projections using paired data, including semi-supervised refinement. Does not test paired-data-free mapping, stitching, relative representations, or loss of each encoder's original utility under mapping.
No recurring interpretable features, neurons, SAE features, or circuits are measured.

Does not compare alternative representation-similarity measures or their settings as measures of convergence. It studies the effect of data source and distribution shift on downstream alignment performance.
Does not isolate shared training data or objectives as causes of convergence, or measure whether alignment plateaus or remains incomplete as models scale.

relationships.condition: Linear maps (Procrustes/CCA/contrastive) fit on 10k CC3M pairs between frozen DINOv3 and NV-Embed-v2
relationships.reason: Closed-form linear maps from 10k pairs reach COCO MeanR@1 21.1-24.2, far above chance (r1-r3). Linear-layer alignment generalizes to SkyScript, speech-text and per-dataset settings (r45-r54).
relationships.display_finding: Closed-form maps fitted on 10,000 pairs achieved COCO MeanR@1 of 21.1–24.2, far above chance, while linear-layer alignment also generalized to SkyScript, speech–text, and per-dataset settings.

source_check.label: supports
source_check.condition: Linear maps (Procrustes/CCA/contrastive) fit on 10k CC3M pairs between frozen DINOv3 and NV-Embed-v2
source_check.reason: Table 1 reports standalone COCO MeanR@1 of 21.1 for Procrustes, 21.5 for CCA and 24.2 for contrastive linear alignment, demonstrating useful cross-modal mapping in this setting.

relationships.condition: Low-supervision linear alignment compared with the 1M-pair supervised upper bound, across encoder pairs
relationships.reason: Even the best 10k-pair maps stay well below 1M-pair SAIL, e.g. COCO T2I R@1 26.5 vs 35.5 and Flickr T2I 51.7 vs 63.1 (r37-r44). Results vary strongly by encoder pair (ImageNet 32.4-46.1, r13-r30). The text reports both methods fail at 100 pairs (Figure 5).
relationships.display_finding: With 10k pairs, COCO text-to-image R@1 was 26.5 versus 35.5 for 1M-pair SAIL and Flickr was 51.7 versus 63.1; ImageNet results ranged from 32.4 to 46.1 across encoder pairs, and both methods failed with 100 pairs.

source_check.label: limits_scope
source_check.condition: Low-supervision linear alignment compared with the 1M-pair supervised upper bound, across encoder pairs
source_check.reason: Tables 4 and 11 show substantial remaining retrieval gaps: SOTAlign versus 1M-pair SAIL is 26.5 versus 35.5 for COCO T2I R@1 and 51.7 versus 63.1 for Flickr30k T2I R@1. Section 6.2 also explicitly reports failure at 100 pairs, qualifying low-loss interchangeability under scarce supervision.

relationships.condition: Raw mutual k-NN of frozen DINOv2 vs DINOv3 ViT-L with each of three fixed text encoders (Table 10, corrected encoder assignment)

relationships.display_finding: DINOv3's mutual k-NN values were 14.1, 18.0 and 17.6 versus DINOv2's 14.6, 18.9 and 18.2 across three text encoders, with these small differences based on only two vision models and no uncertainty estimates.
